transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’ve stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. Salsa nights, church gatherings, cooking for the neighbors... even going into my shop just to smell the wood. None of it feels worth doing lately.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did you first notice you stopped enjoying these activities?
About six months, I’d say. It’s been going on long enough that I know it isn’t just a bad week or regular stress.
Have you ever had a period like this before—months of low mood and loss of interest—prior to these last six months, or is this the first time you've experienced something like this?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another stretch like this before these past six months.
Besides the loss of interest, have you noticed any physical changes recently—like gaining weight without changing your eating habits, feeling unusually cold, or having dry skin or hair?
No, I haven’t really noticed any changes like that.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions recently, or noticed any new problems with your memory, concentration, or thinking clearly?

I haven’t been diagnosed with anything recently. But my thinking’s been off. I’ll look at blueprints I’ve read my whole life, and the lines just blur together in my head. I end up asking the younger guys to explain things I should understand right away.
Did you start noticing this trouble with blueprints and concentration around the same time your mood and interest changes began, or did it start before that?

It started around the same time, I think. I’d stare at blueprints I’ve read my whole life and the lines would just blur together. Then I’d have to ask the younger guys to go over things I should understand right away.
Besides trouble reading blueprints, have you noticed any problems remembering recent conversations or events, or getting confused about places or routines that used to be familiar to you?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed getting confused about where I am or my usual routines.

Have you noticed whether the trouble with blueprints and concentration happens even on days when your mood feels a little better, or does it seem to get worse specifically when you're feeling most down?

It seems worse when I’m really down. I’ll stare at a blueprint I’ve known for years, and the lines just blur together in my head. Then I have to ask the younger guys to explain it again, things I should understand right away.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, such as difficulty falling asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual, since this all began?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid close attention to my sleep, honestly.

On days when your mood feels a bit better, does your ability to read and understand blueprints improve as well, or does that difficulty stay about the same regardless of how you're feeling emotionally?

It does get worse when I’m feeling really down. I’ll look at blueprints I’ve read my whole life and the lines just blur together. Then I’m asking the younger guys to explain things I should understand right away.
Have you experienced any other neurological symptoms recently, such as headaches, weakness, numbness, or changes in your vision, along with the trouble concentrating?
I haven’t really noticed anything else like that. It’s mainly the concentration problem when I’m feeling low.

Besides reading blueprints, have you noticed similar trouble with other complex tasks you used to do easily, like managing your bills, using tools you're familiar with, or following multi-step instructions?

Yeah. It’s mostly at work, but things I’ve done for years don’t click the way they should. I’ll stare at a blueprint and it all just blurs together in my head, then I have to ask the younger guys to repeat something I should’ve understood right away.
Have you been experiencing feelings of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts about death or not wanting to be here during this time?
Yeah... I’ve had thoughts that maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. And sometimes I think my family might be better off without me. It scares me when I catch myself thinking that.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a first-ever episode of pervasive anhedonia and depressed mood lasting 6 months, accompanied by significant cognitive impairment (concentration/executive dysfunction) that fluctuates with mood severity—classic for depressive pseudodementia rather than a primary neurocognitive disorder.
